is: dctx is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Rust context engine for AI-assisted coding: one local binary that packs a project into one structured block, or answers bounded, byte-stable symbol queries (find, read, neighbors, skeleton) as CLI output or MCP tools.
is_not: No RAG: no embeddings, no vector search, and the engine never calls a model.
No network: pack, map, cache and mcp make no network calls; the release check counts socket calls under strace and fails on any.
No agent loop: dctx answers one command at a time; the agent or the human decides what to ask next.

verify_download.available: Each release on GitHub ships prebuilt archives for Linux x64/ARM64, macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64 with a SHA256SUMS file.
verify_download.planned: Signed release binaries and an SBOM are planned; there is no signature to verify yet.

modalities.name: CLI
modalities.line: `dctx pack PATH` for one structured block (clipboard, file or stdout); `dctx map find|read|neighbors|skeleton|...` for bounded symbol answers.

modalities.name: MCP server
modalities.line: `dctx mcp PATH` over stdio for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex; `--profile lean` exposes only find and read.

modalities.name: Task context
modalities.line: `dctx pack --for TEXT --budget N`: find, neighbors and read of the names in TEXT, cut to an estimated-token budget.

modalities.name: CI and prompt cache
modalities.line: Deterministic pack and map output; tree lines carry no timestamps by default, so the prefix stays stable across a touch.

modalities.name: Rust library
modalities.line: The `dctx` facade crate as a tagged Git dependency; crates.io publishing soon.

modalities.name: npm CLI
modalities.line: `npx dctx` runs the native CLI from a Node toolchain once published; use the release archives today.

modalities.name: Desktop app
modalities.line: A Tauri preview you build from source; a GPUI rebuild is planned.

modalities.name: Python and Node libraries
modalities.line: Project-scoped packages with their own pinned binary; not available yet.

scopes: System binary: the `dctx` on PATH belongs to you and your agents, and you upgrade it. Interactive agents and MCP call this one.

Project binary (planned with the Python and Node libraries): a binary installed by a project library lives inside that project (virtualenv, node_modules), pinned and managed by that package manager. Application code and CI call this one; a library never silently falls back to PATH.
Same engine, different owner. Release signing is planned; today both are verified against SHA256SUMS.
notice: dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts the context an agent needs to a fraction. Used without a plan, it can add calls and tokens instead of removing them. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything.

claims.text: A whole-session benchmark against grep plus file reads (every model turn, startup and tool definitions counted) is being prepared and will be published with raw data. No session saving is claimed yet.
Byte stability: the same query on unchanged code returns the same bytes; 33 of 33 text and JSON answers were byte-identical after unrelated edits (Linux only).

The October and November in-house numbers (run 7: 140 of 140 task questions, cold index and warm latency) measure tool output only, as estimated stdout tokens and raw fact coverage without a model; they are not agent completion rates or session costs.
That a pack template changes model answer quality or cost is a hypothesis pending an A/B test; nothing on this site measures it.
